taxonomyNote: NatureServe now includes T. mearnsi in this species (Hope et al. 2016), though ASM and IUCN still recognize it as separate.
fieldMarks: Summer coat reddish- to grayish-brown above with orange chest and belly, unlike its nearest relative the red squirrel
Broad bushy tail with a black tip
Black stripe along the sides, absent in juveniles and faded or absent in winter
Winter coat grayer; ear tufts possible in the far north
behavior: Very vocal, with calls from a low 'chir' to an explosive 'bauf'
Active year round, usually stays in the nest in severe weather; daily activity dawn to sunset
Spring: conifer shoots and bark; fall: cone seeds; stores cones in logs or burrows
Summer nests of twigs and moss; winter nests in tree crevices or underground
habitat: Conifer forest, sea level to 3,300 m; populations generally higher in old growth than younger forest in Washington.
range: Southwestern British Columbia south through the coast ranges, Cascades and Sierra Nevada to southern California and northern Baja California.

lookalikes.name: Red squirrel
lookalikes.howToTell: Lacks the orange chest and belly of Douglas squirrel (ADW).
